title: Unexpected Local Admin Accounts Detected
description: Detects when the LocalAdminAnalyzer flags unexpected local user accounts on the device, including accounts allowed only as standard users that hold local admin rights. This is a known Autopilot bypass technique where admin accounts are created before or during enrollment to gain persistent local admin access.
author: Autopilot Monitor
explanation:
The agent detected unexpected local user accounts on this device: accounts the built-in or tenant-configured allowed list does not allow, or accounts it allows only as standard users that are members of the local Administrators group.

This is a security-relevant finding. Creating local admin accounts before or during Autopilot enrollment is a known bypass technique (e.g. via BypassNRO or Shift+F10 during OOBE) that grants persistent local administrator access.

Click the event link below to jump to the local_admin_analysis event and check: unexpected_accounts (local user accounts not allowed by the list — disabled accounts included, a dormant account can be re-enabled later), unexpected_admin_members (unexpected accounts that are members of the local Administrators group — the actual backdoor), role_violations (accounts allowed only as standard users that are members of Administrators — Windows never puts Guest, kioskUser0 or WsiAccount there), account_details (per account: disabled state, Administrators membership and RID — 500 is the built-in Administrator), unexpected_profiles (C:\Users profile directories not on the allowed list), logged_in_local_accounts (local accounts that were signed in when the shutdown scan ran — a signed-in local account is never exempted, only Entra/domain users are), bypass_nro (whether the BypassNRO registry flag was set), and confidence_score (the agent's confidence in the finding, 0-100).

If these accounts are expected for your environment (e.g. a service account or helpdesk account), add them to the allowed list under Settings → Agent Analyzers. Choose Standard user only for an account that must never be a local administrator.

remediation.title: Review the unexpected accounts
steps: Open the session timeline and locate the local_admin_analysis event
Check the 'unexpected_accounts' and 'unexpected_profiles' lists in the event data
Verify whether these accounts are legitimate for your environment

remediation.title: Add expected accounts to the allowed list (false positive)
steps: Go to Settings → Agent Analyzers section
Under 'Allowed Local Accounts', add the account names that are expected in your environment
Choose 'Standard user only' for an account that must not be a local administrator — it is still reported if it ever joins the Administrators group
Save the settings — future enrollments will no longer flag these accounts

remediation.title: Investigate a potential security issue
steps: Check if the BypassNRO registry flag was set (indicates OOBE was bypassed)
Review the enrollment timeline for Shift+F10 or other OOBE escape indicators

Check 'unexpected_admin_members' and 'account_details' — an unexpected account with Administrators membership is a backdoor even while it is disabled (it can be re-enabled by a scheduled task after enrollment)
Check 'role_violations' — a built-in Windows account or an account you allowed as standard user that sits in Administrators was put there on purpose
Consider re-imaging the device if unauthorized admin access is confirmed
